item.title: The small-model revolution: why the best AI of 2026 runs on your desk
item.dc:creator: NoxaPlus Tech News
item.description: Frontier labs still chase scale, but the most useful products of the year prove that a well-tuned three-billion-parameter model can beat a distant giant on cost, privacy, and latency.

item.title: Local-first is back, and this time it has a business model
item.dc:creator: NoxaPlus Tech News
item.description: Offline-first apps used to be an ideological stance. A new generation of sync engines makes them cheaper to build, easier to trust, and surprisingly sellable.

item.title: The battery is the new benchmark
item.dc:creator: NoxaPlus Tech News
item.description: Phone launches still lead with TOPS and megapixels, but the specification that decides whether a device is good is the one you cannot see on a slide: sustained efficiency.

item.title: The quiet rise of the repairable laptop
item.dc:creator: NoxaPlus Tech News
item.description: Modular ports, standard screws, documented parts, and batteries you can actually replace are moving from enthusiast projects to mainstream purchasing criteria.

item.title: Passkeys are winning quietly. The hard part starts now
item.dc:creator: NoxaPlus Tech News
item.description: Phishing-resistant sign-in is finally normal. The remaining work is account recovery, legacy systems, and the support desk that has to explain it all.

item.title: Small satellites are turning orbit into a data platform
item.dc:creator: NoxaPlus Tech News
item.description: The launch cost story is familiar. The more interesting shift is on the ground, where automated downlink, cloud processing, and subscription analytics are remaking the economics of Earth observation.

item.title: Post-quantum cryptography: a practical migration checklist for small teams
item.dc:creator: NoxaPlus Tech News
item.description: You do not need a quantum computer to start. You need an inventory, crypto agility, and a plan for the data that must stay secret for decades.

item.title: Agents at work: the unglamorous infrastructure that decides who wins
item.dc:creator: NoxaPlus Tech News
item.description: The demo is a model that books a flight. The product is permissions, retries, audit logs, cost controls, and a human who can say no.

item.title: The return of the boring stack
item.dc:creator: NoxaPlus Tech News
item.description: Postgres, server-rendered HTML, a queue, and a monolith are not a compromise anymore. They are a competitive advantage in a world where code is cheap to generate and expensive to understand.

item.title: Satellite messaging is quietly becoming the new roaming
item.dc:creator: NoxaPlus Tech News
item.description: Direct-to-cell coverage is moving from emergency novelty to everyday expectation. The technology is impressive; the business model and the spectrum rules are the hard parts.

item.title: Why lunar software is harder than lunar hardware
item.dc:creator: NoxaPlus Tech News
item.description: A lander can be tested in a vacuum chamber. Its software has to survive radiation, communication gaps, dust, and a two-second round trip that makes every remote fix feel like a negotiation.

item.title: Edge silicon: the chip race moves off the cloud
item.dc:creator: NoxaPlus Tech News
item.description: NPUs are becoming standard equipment, but the winners will be decided by memory bandwidth, thermal design, and whether developers can actually ship to the hardware.
